newsitem.title: USA: Billionaire Harry Helmsley dies at 87.
newsitem.headline: Billionaire Harry Helmsley dies at 87.

text.p: Billionaire Harry Helmsley, one of the richest and most powerful businessmen in New York City real estate, has died at the age of 87.
Helmsley died Saturday afternoon at the Scottsdale Memorial Hospital in Arizona of pneumonia, Howard Rubenstein, Helmsley's New York-based spokesman, said Sunday.
Helmsley's wife, Leona, the self-proclaimed queen of a string of hotels the couple owned, was at his bedside when he died.
"My fairy tale is over. I lived a magical life with Harry," she said in a statement.
The real estate tycoon had been ill for some time and had been hospitalized for about one week, the spokesman said.

His holdings included a partnership in the Empire State Building, which he bought in 1961 for $65 million. He also controlled 27 hotels and 50,000 apartments, and had other real estate holdings in Chicago, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and other cities.
Forbes magazine ranked him as the 67th richest American, putting his net worth at more than $1.7 billion in October 1996.

Helmsley and his wife were indicted in a federal income tax evasion and mail fraud case. The couple was accused of deducting personal expenses for everything from bras to a marble dance floor as business costs in the renovation of their 28-room Greenwich, Conn., mansion that also included a swimming pool and a $130,000 indoor/outdoor stereo system.
Helmsley was ruled unfit to stand trial because of his failing memory and the effects of a stroke. Legal papers said, however, that his wife made the business decisions.

Mrs. Helmsley was convicted in 1989 and given a 32 month sentence at a federal prison and ordered to pay $6.3 million in fines. Her sentence was later reduced to 21 months because of the ill health of her husband. She served 18 months in prison, one month in a Manhattan half-way house and was then confined for two months in her Manhattan penthouse apartment.

During the trial, employees of the couple testified about Mrs. Helmsley's fiery temper and harsh manner. Drawing on her hotel advertising campaign that called her the queen of her hotel empire, Mrs. Helmsley was dubbed "the Queen of Mean."
Helmsley married his wife, the former Leona Mindy Rosenthal, a real estate executive, in 1972 after divorcing his wife of 33 years. It was a second marriage for both. The couple had no children.
A private funeral service for the family will be held, Rubenstein said.
